    return Entry(aro=aro, name=name, short_name=name, model_type=model_type, model_ids=(1,),
                 drug_classes=(), mechanisms=(), gene_families=(),
                 variants=tuple(Variant(m, None) for m in variants), names=tuple([name, *names]))


def reference():
    return Reference([
        entry("ARO:9000001", "mphA"),
        entry("ARO:9000002", "ErmA", names=("ermA",)),
        entry("ARO:9000003", "aadA", names=("aadA, aadA1, aad(3'')(9)",)),
        entry("ARO:9000004", "Staphylococcus aureus gyrA conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones",
              variants=("S84L",)),
        entry("ARO:9000005", "Escherichia coli gyrA conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones",
              variants=("S83L",)),
        entry("ARO:9000006", "Escherichia coli gyrA with mutation conferring resistance to triclosan",
              variants=("G81D",)),
        entry("ARO:9000007", "Escherichia coli parC conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones"),
        entry("ARO:9000008", "CTX-M-15"),
        entry("ARO:9000009", "TEM-1"),
        entry("ARO:9000010", "TEM-2"),
    ], release="card-test")

    bridge = Bridge(reference())
    assert bridge.resolve("mph(A)").entry.aro == "ARO:9000001"
    assert bridge.resolve("erm(A)").entry.aro == "ARO:9000002"
    assert bridge.resolve("mph(A)").how == "normalised_name"


def test_multi_name_synonyms_are_split():
    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("aadA1").entry.aro == "ARO:9000003"


def test_plain_matches_are_untouched():
    res = Bridge(reference()).resolve("CTX-M-15")
    assert (res.status, res.how) == ("resolved", "exact")
    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("blaCTX-M-15").how == "bla_prefix_stripped"


def test_unknown_stays_unknown():
    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("blaZ").status == "unknown"


def test_allele_family_is_not_guessed():

    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("blaTEM").status == "unknown"

    res = Bridge(reference()).resolve("gyrA", "Staphylococcus aureus", "S84L")
    assert (res.status, res.how, res.entry.aro) == ("resolved", "species_variant_model", "ARO:9000004")


def test_point_mutation_without_a_species_does_not_use_a_model():
    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("gyrA", None, "S84L").status == "unknown"


def test_homolog_species_is_labelled_and_used_only_as_a_fallback():
    res = Bridge(reference()).resolve("gyrA", "Klebsiella pneumoniae", "S83L")

    assert res.entry.aro == "ARO:9000005"  # the listed mutation separates the two E. coli models
    assert Bridge(reference()).resolve("parC", "Klebsiella pneumoniae", "S80I").entry.aro == "ARO:9000007"


def test_species_model_beats_homolog():
    res = Bridge(reference()).resolve("gyrA", "Staphylococcus aureus", "S84L")
    assert "homolog" not in res.how


def test_ambiguous_models_are_reported_not_picked():

    assert res.status == "ambiguous" and len(res.candidates) == 2

    parsed = parse_ncbi_genotypes("gyrA_S83Y=POINT,blaSHV-12,mecA=PARTIAL,ompK35_K292QfsTer17=POINT",
                                  Species("Klebsiella pneumoniae"))
    by_raw = {t.raw: t for t in parsed.tokens}
    assert (by_raw["gyrA_S83Y=POINT"].lookup, by_raw["gyrA_S83Y=POINT"].mutation) == ("gyrA", "S83Y")
    assert by_raw["blaSHV-12"].mutation is None and by_raw["mecA=PARTIAL"].method == "amrfinder:PARTIAL"
    assert by_raw["ompK35_K292QfsTer17=POINT"].mutation == "K292QfsTer17"


def test_parse_ncbi_genotypes_reports_what_it_drops():
    parsed = parse_ncbi_genotypes("mecA=PARTIAL,blaZ,blaZ", exclude_methods=("PARTIAL",))

    assert {r.raw for r in parsed.rejected} == {"mecA=PARTIAL", "blaZ"}
    assert parsed.requested == ["mecA=PARTIAL", "blaZ", "blaZ"]

"""WS5b scoring logic on synthetic pairs: counts, metrics, the cluster bootstrap and the freeze."""
import json

import numpy as np
import pytest

from eval import phenotype_validation as pv


def pair(species, cluster, drug, pheno, a="unaffected", b=None):
    status = {arm: a for arm in pv.ARMS}
    if b:
        status["B"] = status["B-intact"] = b
    return {"species": species, "cluster": cluster, "drug": drug, "pheno": pheno, "pool": True, "status": status}


def test_parse_ast_drops_conflicting_calls():
    calls, conflicts = pv.parse_ast("a=R,b=S,a=S,c=I")
    assert calls == {"b": "S", "c": "I"} and conflicts == ["a"]


def test_metrics_from_counts():
    m = pv.metrics([30, 10, 50, 10])  # tp fp tn fn
    assert m["sensitivity"] == pytest.approx(0.75)
    assert m["specificity"] == pytest.approx(50 / 60)
    assert m["ppv_ruled_out"] == pytest.approx(0.75)
    assert m["false_reassurance"] == pytest.approx(10 / 60)
    assert m["balanced_accuracy"] == pytest.approx((0.75 + 50 / 60) / 2)


def test_prediction_rules():
    p = pair("klebsiella", "c1", "MEROPENEM", "R", a="partly_affected")
    prior = {("klebsiella", "MEROPENEM"): "S"}
    assert pv.prediction(p, "A|class", prior) == "R"
    assert pv.prediction(p, "A|strict", prior) == "S"
    assert pv.prediction(p, "never_ruled_out", prior) == "S"
    assert pv.prediction(p, "drug_prior", prior) == "S"


def test_drug_prior_tie_predicts_susceptible():
    pairs = [pair("klebsiella", "c1", "X", "R"), pair("klebsiella", "c2", "X", "S")]
    assert pv.drug_prior(pairs)[("klebsiella", "X")] == "S"


def perfect_and_noisy():
    pairs = []
    for sp in pv.SPECIES:
        for k in range(12):
            res = k % 2 == 0
            pairs.append(pair(sp, f"{sp}{k}", "D", "R" if res else "S", a="defeated" if res else "unaffected"))
            pairs.append(pair(sp, f"{sp}{k}", "E", "R" if res else "S", a="defeated" if res else "unaffected"))
    return pairs


def test_perfect_rule_scores_perfectly_and_beats_the_never_baseline():
    out = pv.evaluate_scope(perfect_and_noisy(), "pool")
    a = out["strata"]["pooled"]["A|class"]
    assert a["balanced_accuracy"]["value"] == 1.0 and a["false_reassurance"]["value"] == 0.0
    assert out["strata"]["pooled"]["never_ruled_out"]["balanced_accuracy"]["value"] == 0.5
    assert out["differences"]["pooled"]["A-class minus drug_prior"]["value"] > 0


def test_bootstrap_is_reproducible_and_clustered():
    one, two = pv.evaluate_scope(perfect_and_noisy(), "pool"), pv.evaluate_scope(perfect_and_noisy(), "pool")
    assert one == two
    # three species with 12 clusters each: the pooled count reflects whole clusters only
    cells = pv.cluster_counts(perfect_and_noisy(), "pool")["klebsiella"]["A|class"]
    assert cells.shape == (12, 4) and cells.sum() == 24


def test_a_useless_rule_has_no_signal():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    pairs = [pair(sp, f"{sp}{k % 15}", f"D{k % 3}", "R" if rng.random() < .5 else "S",
                  a="defeated" if rng.random() < .5 else "unaffected")
             for sp in pv.SPECIES for k in range(300)]
    pooled = pv.evaluate_scope(pairs, "pool")["strata"]["pooled"]["A|class"]["balanced_accuracy"]
    assert pooled["ci95"][0] < 0.5 < pooled["ci95"][1]


def test_catalogue_scope_includes_drugs_outside_the_pool():
    pairs = [pair("klebsiella", "c1", "COLISTIN", "R", a="defeated")]
    pairs[0]["pool"] = False
    assert pv.evaluate_scope(pairs, "pool")["strata"]["klebsiella"]["A|class"]["n_pairs"] == 0
    assert pv.evaluate_scope(pairs, "catalogue")["strata"]["klebsiella"]["A|class"]["n_pairs"] == 1


def test_freeze_verify_amend(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    for rel in pv.FROZEN_FILES.values():
        f = tmp_path / rel
        f.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        f.write_text("x")
    out = tmp_path / "pre.json"
    pv.freeze(tmp_path, out)
    assert pv.verify(tmp_path, out) == []
    (tmp_path / pv.FROZEN_FILES["protocol"]).write_text("changed")
    assert pv.verify(tmp_path, out) == ["protocol changed since the freeze"]
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        pv.freeze(tmp_path, out)  # a freeze is not redone
    record = pv.amend("fix", tmp_path, out)
    assert record["amendments"][0]["changed"] == ["protocol"] and pv.verify(tmp_path, out) == []
    assert json.loads(out.read_text())["sha256"]["protocol"] != record["amendments"][0]["sha256"]["protocol"]

# WS5b phenotype validation — pre-registered protocol

**No result has been produced when this file is frozen.** No prediction has been compared with a
measured phenotype. This is a second, larger test beside the three-row
[retrospective protocol](../ws5_retrospective/protocol.md), which it does not replace or alter.

## Question

For an isolate's resistance genes, does the evasion rule's "ruled out" verdict match the
susceptibility the laboratory measured for the same isolate and drug?

The rule is the one the ranking uses ([evasion.py](../../core/ranking/antibiotic/evasion.py)): a
drug is `defeated` when CARD names it for a gene in the profile, `partly_affected` when CARD links
only its class, `unaffected` when neither, `unknown` when the drug has no CARD class. Nothing about
efficacy, dosing or treatment is tested.

## Data

NCBI Pathogen Detection, `latest_snps/AMR/*.amr.metadata.tsv`, downloaded 8 November 2026 for
*K. pneumoniae* (PDG000000012.2573), *A. baumannii* (PDG000000010.1996) and *S. aureus*
(PDG000000073.1326). Each row carries the AMRFinderPlus genes (`AMR_genotypes_core`) and the
laboratory susceptibility calls (`AST_phenotypes`, e.g. `meropenem=R`). Files are pinned by sha256
at freeze time.

- Rows whose `scientific_name` starts with the species binomial and whose `AST_phenotypes` is not
  `NULL`. One row per `biosample_acc` (first kept).
- An isolate with `AMR_genotypes_core` `NULL` and `number_core_amr_genes` 0 has a measured empty
  gene set. It is scored with an empty profile, where every drug is `unaffected`. An isolate with
  `NULL` genotypes and a nonzero gene count is excluded and counted.
- Phenotype calls: `R` and `S` are scored. `I` is counted and not scored. `ND`, `NS`, `DD` and any
  other value are counted and not scored.

## Pairs, drugs and scope

A *pair* is one isolate and one drug with an `R` or `S` call. The AST drug name is mapped to a
catalogue drug by [drug_map.json](drug_map.json), written from names alone. Combination products,
veterinary agents and drugs absent from the catalogue are not scored and their pair counts are
reported by reason.

- **Primary scope**: the 126 approved single agents the ranking offers (`load_pool`).
- **Secondary scope**: all 227 catalogue drugs (`load_pool(approved_only=False)`), which adds
  colistin, polymyxin B and gentamicin.
- A pair whose drug has no CARD class (`unknown`) is not scored, in every arm, so every arm and
  every baseline sees the same pairs.

## Method arms

Genes enter as the product would receive them: each AMRFinderPlus symbol becomes a determinant,
a `POINT` symbol is split into gene and mutation (`parse_ncbi_genotypes`), and the profile is built
with `build_profile` against the pinned CARD 4.0.2 release with its curated supplement.

| Arm | Resolver | Calls included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** (primary) | CARD name matching as shipped | all core calls |
| **B** | A, then the bridge ([bridge.py](../../core/resistance/htb_resistance/bridge.py)): normalised spelling, and species variant models | all core calls |
| **A-intact** | as A | calls with method `PARTIAL`, `PARTIAL_END_OF_CONTIG`, `MISTRANSLATION`, `HMM` removed |
| **B-intact** | as B | same removal |

A is primary because it is the tool as it existed when this protocol was written. B is the
improvement written while preparing this test and is reported with equal prominence. The bridge was
developed by looking at which gene symbols failed to resolve, using genotypes of these same
isolates and **no phenotypes**; its rules are mechanical, contain no per-gene alias, and are frozen
here by hash. A gene that does not resolve is simply absent from the profile (it is recorded in
`unresolved_inputs`, as the tool does).

## Prediction

- **Ruled out** (primary rule): status `defeated` or `partly_affected`.
- **Not ruled out**: status `unaffected`.
- Strict variant, reported beside it: ruled out only when `defeated`.

Ruled out predicts `R`. Not ruled out predicts `S`.

## Metrics

Primary: **balanced accuracy**, (sensitivity + specificity) / 2, with `R` as the positive class,
for arm A, the primary rule, primary scope, pooled over the three species.

Always reported, not selected afterwards:

- sensitivity (share of `R` pairs ruled out) and specificity (share of `S` pairs not ruled out)
- **`ppv_ruled_out`**: of pairs ruled out, the share that are `R`
- **`false_reassurance`**: of pairs not ruled out, the share that are `R`. This is the wrong answer
  that matters: a drug presented as unaffected that the laboratory found resistant. It is reported
  even when balanced accuracy looks acceptable.
- the share of pairs with a verdict other than `unknown` (coverage), and gene-call resolution rates
  per arm

The metric set above is complete. Anything else is an observation, never the headline.

## Baselines

Run on the same pairs.

- **never_ruled_out**: predicts `S` for every pair (balanced accuracy 0.5 by construction).
- **drug_prior**: for each species and drug, predict that pair's majority phenotype. It is fitted
  on the same pairs it is scored on, which **flatters** it. A rule that cannot beat it adds nothing
  beyond knowing which drug and which species.

## Uncertainty

Cluster bootstrap, 2000 resamples, 95% percentile interval, seed `20261108`. The cluster is the
`bioproject_acc`, resampled with replacement within each species, then pooled. Isolates from one
study share laboratory, breakpoints and often ancestry, so resampling isolates would overstate
precision. Rule and baseline are scored on the same resample, so the *difference* in balanced
accuracy (arm minus drug_prior, and B minus A) has its own interval.

The clusters are uneven (629 of the 1,143 *A. baumannii* isolates come from one bioproject), so the
intervals will be wide for that species. That is the honest result.

## Decision rules (fixed now)

1. The rule **carries signal** only if the lower bound of arm A's pooled balanced accuracy exceeds 0.5.
2. The rule **adds information beyond the drug** only if the lower bound of (A − drug_prior) exceeds 0.
3. B **improves on** A only if the lower bound of (B − A) exceeds 0.
4. A negative result stands and is the finding. Nothing is re-run with different settings after
   the result is seen. A run that fails or is abandoned is reported.

## What this cannot show

- AST labels come from many laboratories, methods and breakpoint editions. The NCBI set is not a
  random sample of isolates (it over-represents resistant ones), so prevalence-dependent numbers
  such as `ppv_ruled_out` describe this collection, not a hospital.
- A gene's presence is not expression (the tool's own caveat). AMRFinderPlus gene calls are
  themselves predictions.
- CARD links genes to drug *classes*; a drug sharing a class with one the gene defeats is scored as
  ruled out whether or not that drug is affected.
- A genotype that resolves to nothing is treated as no determinant, so unresolved genes lower
  sensitivity. Arms A and B measure that cost.
- The test was designed knowing the overall counts of `R` and `S` per species and the AST drug
  names, which were printed while checking the file format. No prediction had been compared
  with any phenotype.
- This tests the evasion rule only, not the ordering of the remaining drugs and not any generated
  molecule.

## Amendments

None. Changes are recorded by `python -m eval.phenotype_validation --amend` with a reason, which
appends to `preregistered.json` and leaves the original declaration intact.

lines: - An isolate with `AMR_genotypes_core` `NULL` and `number_core_amr_genes` 0 has a measured empty
gene set. It is scored with an empty profile, where every drug is `unaffected`. An isolate with
`NULL` genotypes and a nonzero gene count is excluded and counted.
+- A drug listed more than once for an isolate with different calls (repeat testing that disagrees)
+  is dropped for that isolate and counted, not resolved in either direction.
- Phenotype calls: `R` and `S` are scored. `I` is counted and not scored. `ND`, `NS`, `DD` and any
other value are counted and not scored.

    if settings.repo == "memory":

    assert settings.database_url is not None  # Settings refuses postgres without one

def build_components(
    settings: Settings,
    *,
    repo: Repo | None = None,
    source: ExperimentSource | None = None,
    jury: JuryBackend | None = None,
    docking: DockingBackend | None = None,
    evaluation: EvaluationSource | None = None,
    molecules: MoleculeSource | None = None,
    resistance: ResistanceSource | None = None,
    runner: Runner | None = None,
) -> Components:
    """Fixture-mode pieces by default; any piece can be replaced. Opens the database
    when the settings say postgres and no repo is given."""
    fixtures = settings.fixtures_dir
    opened = repo is None
    repo = repo or open_repo(settings)
    try:
        jury = jury or open_jury(settings, repo)
        # Vina mode reads each structure's measured control from the repo.
        docking = docking or open_docking(settings, repo)
        source = source or open_source(settings, docking)
        seed_dock_jobs(repo, docking)
    except Exception:
        if opened:
            repo.close()
        raise
    jobs = JobFactory(repo=repo, source=source, jury=jury, docking=docking)
    if runner is None:
        if isinstance(repo, PostgresRepo):
            runner = PostgresQueue(repo)
        else:
            runner = ThreadRunner(jobs, settings.fixture_delay_ms, settings.worker_threads)
    return Components(
        settings=settings,
        repo=repo,
        source=source,
        jury=jury,
        docking=docking,
        evaluation=evaluation or FixtureEvaluation(fixtures),
        molecules=molecules or open_molecules(settings),
        resistance=resistance
        or (
            SavedResistance(fixtures, settings.data_dir, settings.resistance_results_dir)
            if settings.resistance == "saved"
            else CardResistance(fixtures, settings.data_dir)
        ),
        runner=runner,
        jobs=jobs,
    )

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from htb_api.app import create_app
from htb_api.services.resistance import SavedResistance
from htb_api.settings import FIXTURES_DIR, REPO_ROOT, Settings

BUNDLE = REPO_ROOT / "results" / "pathogen-integration"


def test_saved_rankings_through_api() -> None:
    with TestClient(create_app(Settings(resistance="saved", fixture_delay_ms=0))) as client:
        presets = client.get("/api/resistance/pathogens").json()["items"]
        assert len(presets) == 3
        certificates = client.get("/api/resistance/certificates").json()["certificates"]
        assert certificates and all(c["ran"] and c["lean_version"] for c in certificates)
        for preset in presets:
            profile_id = preset["profile_id"]
            profile = client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{profile_id}").json()
            response = client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{profile_id}/candidates")
            assert response.status_code == 200
            result = response.json()
            assert result["profile_id"] == profile["profile_id"]
            assert result["pathogen"] == profile["input"]["species"]
            assert result["fixture_note"] is None
            assert len(result["candidates"]) == 126
            # Lean ran on every molecule; a molecule outside the limits is "failed", never silent.
            assert {c["certificate_status"] for c in result["candidates"]} <= {"certified", "failed"}
            assert all(
                c["certificate"]["ran"] and c["certificate"]["inchikey"] == c["inchikey"]
                for c in result["candidates"]
            )
            assert any(
                e["source"] == "htb_resistance" for c in result["candidates"] for e in c["evidence"]
            )
            levels = {"unaffected": 0, "unknown": 1, "partly_affected": 2, "defeated": 3}
            order = [levels[c["evasion"]["status"]] for c in result["candidates"]]
            assert order == sorted(order)
        assert client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{uuid4()}").status_code == 404


def test_corrupt_saved_bundle_fails_closed(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copytree(BUNDLE, tmp_path / "bundle")
    path = tmp_path / "bundle" / "staphylococcus-aureus.ranking.json"
    content = json.loads(path.read_text())
    content["candidates"][0]["name"] = "corrupted"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(content))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="checksum mismatch"):
        SavedResistance(FIXTURES_DIR, tmp_path, path.parent)

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from htb_api.app import create_app
from htb_api.services.resistance import SavedResistance
from htb_api.settings import FIXTURES_DIR, REPO_ROOT, Settings

BUNDLE = REPO_ROOT / "results" / "pathogen-integration"


def test_saved_rankings_through_api() -> None:
    with TestClient(create_app(Settings(resistance="saved", fixture_delay_ms=0))) as client:
        presets = client.get("/api/resistance/pathogens").json()["items"]
        assert len(presets) == 3
        certificates = client.get("/api/resistance/certificates").json()["certificates"]
        assert certificates and all(c["ran"] and c["lean_version"] for c in certificates)
        for preset in presets:
            profile_id = preset["profile_id"]
            profile = client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{profile_id}").json()
            response = client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{profile_id}/candidates")
            assert response.status_code == 200
            result = response.json()
            assert result["profile_id"] == profile["profile_id"]
            assert result["pathogen"] == profile["input"]["species"]
            assert result["fixture_note"] is None
            assert len(result["candidates"]) == 126
            # Lean ran on every molecule; a molecule outside the limits is "failed", never silent.
            assert {c["certificate_status"] for c in result["candidates"]} <= {"certified", "failed"}
            assert all(
                c["certificate"]["ran"] and c["certificate"]["inchikey"] == c["inchikey"]
                for c in result["candidates"]
            )
            assert any(
                e["source"] == "htb_resistance" for c in result["candidates"] for e in c["evidence"]
            )
            levels = {"unaffected": 0, "unknown": 1, "partly_affected": 2, "defeated": 3}
            order = [levels[c["evasion"]["status"]] for c in result["candidates"]]
            assert order == sorted(order)
        assert client.get(f"/api/resistance/profiles/{uuid4()}").status_code == 404


def test_corrupt_saved_bundle_fails_closed(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copytree(BUNDLE, tmp_path / "bundle")
    path = tmp_path / "bundle" / "staphylococcus-aureus.ranking.json"
    content = json.loads(path.read_text())
    content["candidates"][0]["name"] = "corrupted"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(content))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="checksum mismatch"):
        SavedResistance(FIXTURES_DIR, tmp_path, path.parent)

from pathlib import Path
p=Path("docs/limits.md"); s=p.read_text()

old_end=s.index("### Resistance data")
new='''### Validation: measured against laboratory susceptibility, and what it found

**The ordered ranking of the approved antibiotics has still not been scored against known outcomes.** The three-row retrospective test ([protocol](../results/ws5_retrospective/protocol.md), #37) has no result, so no hits@k or MRR figure exists and none should be quoted.

**The evasion rule has been compared with measured susceptibility.** [WS5b](../results/ws5_phenotype_validation/results.md) (pre-registered and frozen before any result, [protocol](../results/ws5_phenotype_validation/protocol.md)) takes 5,067 NCBI Pathogen Detection isolates of the three pathogens, runs each isolate's AMRFinderPlus genes through the profile and the rule, and compares "ruled out" with the laboratory's R or S for the same drug: 41,354 isolate-drug pairs over the 126 approved antibiotics. Intervals are cluster bootstraps over study (bioproject).

| | Balanced accuracy (95% CI) | Gene resolver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rule as shipped (arm A, primary) | 70.5% (61.6–77.7) | CARD name matching |
| Rule with the bridge (arm B) | 75.5% (66.1–83.3) | adds spelling normalisation and species point-mutation models |
| "Know the drug and species" baseline | 75.4% (67.0–80.6) | none (fitted on the same pairs, so it flatters itself) |

What that means, in the order the protocol fixed:

- **The rule carries signal** (lower bound 61.6%, above 50%).
- **It does not add information beyond knowing the drug and species** (A minus baseline: −4.9 points, interval −10.8 to +2.3). For *K. pneumoniae* (61.9% against 60.9%) and *A. baumannii* (53.2% against 67.0%) it does no better than that baseline. Both collections are mostly multidrug-resistant, so "most drugs are resisted" is already a strong guess. For *S. aureus* it does better: 71.0% against 58.9% as shipped, and 89.4% with the bridge.
- **"Unaffected" is not reassurance.** Of the drugs the rule left unaffected, 28.6% (13.9–49.6) were resistant as shipped, and 13.8% (3.2–32.4) with the bridge.
- **The bridge helps** (B minus A: +4.9 points, +2.5 to +7.3), mainly because unresolved genes were silently missing (A resolves 65% of gene calls, B 83%). That is a gain on the shipped resolver, not on the baseline.
- **Where it over-calls.** Ruling out by class makes specificity low for the Gram-negatives (27% for *K. pneumoniae* as shipped). An exploratory look (not pre-registered, [observations](../results/ws5_phenotype_validation/observations.md)) found the false "ruled out" calls come from intrinsic or regulatory determinants: chromosomal SHV-1 and OqxAB in *K. pneumoniae*, OXA-66 in *A. baumannii*, blaR1 in *S. aureus*. A gene being in CARD is not the isolate being resistant.

What this does not show: it is the rule only, not the ordering that follows it, and it says nothing about whether any drug cures anything. The NCBI collection over-represents resistant isolates; the laboratory labels come from many sites and breakpoint editions; 629 of the 1,143 *A. baumannii* isolates come from one study. Combination products (piperacillin-tazobactam, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole), imipenem and rifampin are not in the catalogue, so 8,326 of the available pairs were not scored.

'''
s=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]

# app section
a=s.index("### The app shows fixture rankings"); b=s.index("### The model jury")
s=s[:a]+'''### The app shows fixture rankings unless told otherwise

By default the API serves a fixture ranking, and its candidate result carries a `fixture_note` saying so. With `HTB_RESISTANCE=live` (and a built CARD release and catalogue, `HTB_RESISTANCE_CATALOGUE_DIR`), a profile built from typed genes or a preset is ranked from that profile on request, with no `fixture_note`. Typed genes then need one of the three supported species, named or by alias (`MRSA`, `K. pneumoniae`); a mutation is written `gyrA S84L`. Lean is not run in live mode (certificates stay `not_run`) and ChEMBL activity is included only when `HTB_RESISTANCE_CHEMBL_DB` is set. A demo that does not use live mode must not describe its shortlist as computed from the profile on screen. Pasting AMRFinderPlus output is not yet an input the API accepts (it would add an input kind to the contract).

'''+s[b:]

# table
s=s.replace("| No validation result | #37: freeze the protocol on the evaluation machine, then run and publish |","| Ranking not scored against known outcomes | #37: freeze the protocol on the evaluation machine, then run and publish. The evasion rule alone is covered by WS5b above |")
s=s.replace("| App shows fixture rankings | Calling the ranking from the API; #34 produced the rankings but not that wiring |","| App shows fixture rankings | Run the API with `HTB_RESISTANCE=live` |\n| Class-level over-calling from intrinsic and regulatory genes | Treating chromosomal and regulatory determinants separately; a cited list is needed, none exists yet |\n| `blaZ` and bare allele families (`blaTEM`, `blaOXA`) do not resolve | A cited curated alias; CARD holds them only as families |")
p.write_text(s)
E
grep -n "validated\|unvalidated" docs/limits.md | head

5:The short version: **this tool proposes which antibiotics are not known to be defeated by an isolate's resistance mechanisms, and shows its working. It does not predict that any drug will cure anything, and it has not yet been validated against known outcomes.**
74:The redocking controls are defined but their results are measured by the docking worker at runtime and are not recorded in the repository, so **whether each structure reproduces its crystal pose within 2 Å is not currently stated anywhere**. Until it is, the structures are prepared rather than validated.
106:> It takes an isolate's resistance genes, works out which drug classes known mechanisms rule out, and ranks the approved antibiotics that remain — showing the CARD evidence, the property checks and an independent model panel's reading of the same evidence. The ranking has not yet been validated against known outcomes, and the shortlist currently shown in the app is fixture data.

Steps 1 and 2 are done, and step 3 is partly done. The headline result is that the rule beats chance but doesn't beat a drug-and-species baseline for two of the three pathogens.

## Step 1: validation against measured susceptibility
I pre-registered and froze a protocol before scoring anything ([protocol.md](results/ws5_phenotype_validation/protocol.md)). I then compared the rule's "ruled out" verdict with laboratory R/S calls for 5,067 NCBI isolates, 41,354 isolate-drug pairs. Full output is in [results.md](results/ws5_phenotype_validation/results.md).

| | Balanced accuracy (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| Rule as shipped | 70.5% (61.6–77.7) |
| Rule with the new bridge | 75.5% (66.1–83.3) |
| Know the drug and species | 75.4% (67.0–80.6) |

- **Signal:** the rule does carry signal.
- **No gain over the baseline:** it adds nothing beyond knowing the drug and species for *K. pneumoniae* and *A. baumannii*. For *S. aureus* it does (71% as shipped, 89% with the bridge, against 59%).
- **False reassurance:** of drugs left "unaffected", 28.6% were resistant as shipped, and 13.8% with the bridge.
- **Where it over-calls:** in a post-hoc, non-pre-registered look ([observations.md](results/ws5_phenotype_validation/observations.md)), most false "ruled out" calls came from intrinsic or regulatory genes such as SHV-1, OqxAB, OXA-66 and blaR1.
- **Caveats:** the baseline is fitted on the same pairs, so it flatters itself. The collection over-represents resistant isolates. 629 of the 1,143 *A. baumannii* isolates come from one study.

## Step 2: the API ranks from the profile
`HTB_RESISTANCE=live` builds a profile from typed genes or a preset and ranks the 126 approved drugs from it, with no `fixture_note`. The web app needed no change. Typed genes need one of the three species, named or by alias (for example `MRSA`).

Two bugs turned up along the way. Typed profiling returned 503 with default settings because it looked in `data/releases` instead of `data/card/releases`. A typed gene list also failed on a missing taxid. Both are fixed, and I made one existing test independent of what's on the machine.

## Step 3: mutations (partly done)
A new resolver ([bridge.py](core/resistance/htb_resistance/bridge.py)) resolves point mutations like `gyrA S84L` against the species-specific CARD models. It also normalises spellings like `mph(A)`. For *K. pneumoniae* gyrA and parC it borrows the *E. coli* model, and says so in the profile. Mutant docking isn't done.

## Things to know
- **Tests:** the API suite passes. Five existing core "real run" tests still fail because `data/antibiotics/` holds a 3-drug excerpt. They aren't affected by my changes, and I left that directory alone. The full catalogue I rebuilt is in `data/antibiotics_full/`.
- **Still unresolved:** `blaZ` and bare allele families like `blaTEM` stay unresolved, since fixing them needs a cited alias table.
- **Git:** nothing is committed. Several files, including `services/resistance.py`, show as already staged, which I didn't do.
- **Docs:** [docs/limits.md](docs/limits.md) and the README row are updated to match the results.

# Environment update
 - Primary working directory: /Users/tomato/Developer/GitHub/HTB26-Main/data/wholecell/models (was /Users/tomato/Developer/GitHub/HTB26-Main)

I'm assuming "newer GNN" means the organism-specific Chemprop ensembles trained recently, since the repo has no other newer graph model. Say so if you meant something else.

**K. pneumoniae ensemble** (`mic_573_scaffold`, scaffold split, 5 members, trained on ChEMBL MIC data; [eval.json](data/wholecell/models/mic_573_scaffold/eval.json)). The ensemble is the same Chemprop model type as before, with an RDKit 2D descriptor featurizer.

| | ROC-AUC (95% CI) | PR-AUC (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| Ensemble | 0.863 (0.849–0.877) | 0.761 (0.737–0.784) |
| Nearest-active Tanimoto baseline | 0.842 (0.826–0.858) | 0.661 (0.632–0.693) |

- **This is much tighter than the *A. baumannii* model.** That one had 21 test actives and an interval of 0.58–0.82. This test set has 3,270 compounds and 960 actives, so the interval is about ±0.014.
- **The PR-AUC gap over the baseline is probably real.** The intervals don't overlap (0.761 against 0.661). The ROC-AUC intervals do overlap slightly, so I wouldn't claim that difference.
- **The members are consistent.** Their ROC-AUCs run from 0.844 to 0.864.

Four caveats:

1. **The tight interval is optimistic.** It resamples individual compounds, but compounds from the same series are correlated. A bootstrap over scaffold clusters would be wider. This is the same issue I used bioprojects to handle in the phenotype validation.
2. **It is a leakier "scaffold" test than the *A. baumannii* one.** 74% of test compounds have a training neighbour above 0.5 Tanimoto, against 52% before, so 0.86 isn't a "new chemistry" number.
3. **It isn't comparable to the *A. baumannii* result.** The task is different: literature ChEMBL MICs with a 29% active rate, against a 1.4% screening hit rate, and the labels come from published papers.
4. **It says nothing about resistance.** It predicts growth inhibition of a *K. pneumoniae* strain, not activity against resistant isolates.

**S. aureus ensemble** (`mic_1280_scaffold`) has only `member_0` and no `eval.json`, so it has no interval yet. It looks like it was still training when I checked.

I haven't re-run anything. These numbers are read from the files on disk. I can add a scaffold-cluster bootstrap for the *K. pneumoniae* result to get a more honest interval.

content.text:
Both changes are done, and the API on port 8000 has been restarted with them.

**Copy removed.** I deleted "The server looks each name up in CARD…" from [en.ts](app/web/src/copy/en.ts) and from the gene field in [PathogenInput.tsx](app/web/src/steps/PathogenInput.tsx), including its accessibility link. I updated the one test that read it. Typecheck is clean and the component tests pass.

**Lean now runs for real.** I used the Lean tool rather than relabelling:
- **Live mode:** it now runs Lean 4 (4.35.0) over each molecule's property rules.
- **Results:** 119 of the 126 drugs come back `certified` and 7 come back `failed`, for all three pathogens. The 7 are drugs outside the encoded limits, such as vancomycin. Every candidate now has a status, and none read "not run".
- **Certificates page:** it lists 126 certificates produced by Lean itself, never a fixture's.
- **Speed and caching:** the first build takes about 5 seconds and later builds use the cache at `data/lean-certificates.json`.
- **Settings:** it is on by default. `HTB_RESISTANCE_LEAN=0` turns it off, and if Lean isn't installed the candidates read `unavailable`.

A "certified" label means only that the six encoded property rules hold. It says nothing about safety or activity, and [docs/limits.md](docs/limits.md) says so.

The API tests I re-ran pass (58): live resistance, the existing resistance tests and the saved-resistance tests. I did not re-run the full suites after this change.

One thing to watch for: the "Lean was not run" wording in the profile caveats only appears in saved mode, which this server no longer uses. It would show again if you switch back to saved mode.

content.text:
The demo table now shows real activity and a more informative property check. I did both of the things you suggested: Lean actually runs, and activity is checked against ChEMBL.

**Activity (was "Not measured")**
- **Source:** the live API now reads the ChEMBL database that was already on this machine and loads median MICs for the profile's species. This is cached per species, so it costs about 2 seconds once.
- **Coverage:** 87 of 126 drugs have a MIC for *S. aureus*, 73 for *K. pneumoniae* and 49 for *A. baumannii*.
- **Ranking:** the order is now driven by potency. For the MRSA preset, garenoxacin (0.05 mg/L) comes first and dalbavancin (0.06) second. For *K. pneumoniae* it is plazomicin, then netilmicin.
- **Rows without a MIC:** these now read "No MIC in ChEMBL", because ChEMBL simply has no record. That is more accurate than "Not measured". Sulfonamides will mostly still show this.

**Property check (was "Lean 4 certificate proved")**
- **Wording:** the last column now says what was checked: "All 6 limits met · Lean 4 proved", or "Over limit: weight, polar surface · Lean 4 refuted". If Lean didn't run, it says "Python check only".
- **Why the verdicts are real:** Lean runs for real, so these are real proofs. Each one is a proof of the six encoded limits, not of safety or activity.
- **Limit of the column:** 119 of 126 rows still show "All 6 limits met". That column won't differentiate drugs much.

**Where it's running:** I restarted the API on port 8000 (live mode, same environment as before). The Vite dev servers should hot-reload the new wording at http://localhost:5173.

**Tests:** I re-ran the frontend suite (285 pass) and the live-resistance API tests (5 pass). I did not re-run the full API suite after this change.

If you want the table to say more, I could show the MIC next to the rank, or hide drugs with no MIC behind a filter. A MIC-ceiling filter already exists in the page.

"""The leakage assertion: crash before any evaluation if a held-out compound has leaked (issue #84).

A held-out compound has leaked if it, or any analogue above ``THRESHOLD`` Tanimoto similarity
(Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits, the setting the abaucin paper's own nearest-neighbour script uses),
appears in any of the four sets the spec names: the training set, the calibration set, the
generator's seed fragments, or the nearest-neighbour baseline's reference set.

It fails closed: all four sets must be passed, even when one is empty, so a forgotten set is an
error rather than a silent pass. Exact matches are caught by InChIKey as well as by similarity.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from rdkit import Chem, DataStructs, RDLogger
from rdkit.Chem import rdFingerprintGenerator

from .chem import standardise

RDLogger.DisableLog("rdApp.*")

THRESHOLD = 0.5
REQUIRED_SETS = ("training", "calibration", "generator_seeds", "baseline_reference")
_GEN = rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048)


class LeakageError(AssertionError):
    """A held-out compound or a close analogue is in a set it must not be in."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Leak:
    held_out: str
    set_name: str
    member: str
    similarity: float


def fingerprint(smiles: str):

content.text:
Leakage is handled the same way everywhere: decide what unit must never cross between train and test, split on it before looking at results, and make the code refuse to run if it crosses. This repo already follows that pattern in one place and has gaps in others.

**Already in place**
- **Hidden-drug test:** [leakage.py](core/wholecell/htb_wholecell/leakage.py) crashes if a held-out compound, or anything above 0.5 Tanimoto to it, is in the training set, the calibration set, the generator's seeds or the baseline reference set. It checks all four and fails closed.
- **Splits:** scaffold, random and year splits exist, and a scaffold-disjointness assertion guards them.
- **Pre-registration:** the retrospective and phenotype protocols were frozen by hash before any result.

**Gaps, in order of how much they matter for the demo**

1. **The *K. pneumoniae* and *S. aureus* ensembles.** Their "scaffold" test set is leaky: 74% of test compounds have a training neighbour above 0.5 Tanimoto. The 0.86 AUC mostly reflects near-duplicates.
   - **Fix:** split by similarity cluster (Butina at about 0.5), not by Murcko scaffold. Also split by source document, so one paper's series don't land on both sides.
   - **Reporting:** report results by nearest-neighbour band, as the transfer tests already do with "no close training analogue". The headline should be the far band.
   - **Intervals:** bootstrap over clusters.
2. **Activity feeding the ranking.** The ranking uses ChEMBL MICs, and the retrospective ground truth comes from the same literature. A drug that is "effective" because of published MICs is also ranked high by them. The protocol's `evasion_only` baseline separates this, so keep it prominent, and exclude any ChEMBL records from documents cited in the ground truth.
3. **The phenotype validation.**
   - **Circularity:** CARD and the lab labels share sources, and the bridge was designed on the same isolates' genotypes. I disclosed that.
   - **Fix:** if you tune anything further, tune on a few bioprojects and test on the rest. Don't reuse the frozen test.
4. **The generator guide.** It is trained on `liu_train`, whose labels come from the abaucin screen. Hidden compounds are purged and asserted. The remaining risk is that the guide is guided toward that screen's own definition of "active".
5. **Calibration versus test.** Keep the conformal calibration set disjoint from the test set.

Which one do you mean? I'd start with the *K. pneumoniae* ensemble, since it's the one with a headline number that looks better than it should. I can build the similarity-cluster split, retrain, and report by similarity band with cluster-bootstrap intervals. Retraining takes about 2 hours for 5 members.

"""Tests for scaffold splits and the leakage assertion (#84)."""

import random

import pytest

from htb_wholecell import leakage, split

ABAUCIN = "O=C1Nc2ccccc2C2(CCN(CCc3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)CC2)O1"      # the held-out compound
ANALOGUE = "O=C1Nc2ccccc2C2(CCN(CCc3ccc(C(F)(F)Cl)cc3)CC2)O1"    # CF3 -> CF2Cl, a close analogue
UNRELATED = ["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"]


def _sets(**override):
    sets = {name: list(UNRELATED) for name in leakage.REQUIRED_SETS}
    sets.update(override)
    return sets


def test_the_analogue_really_is_above_the_threshold():
    from rdkit import DataStructs
    sim = DataStructs.TanimotoSimilarity(leakage.fingerprint(ABAUCIN), leakage.fingerprint(ANALOGUE))
    assert sim > leakage.THRESHOLD, "fixture is wrong: the planted analogue must be a leak"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("set_name", leakage.REQUIRED_SETS)
def test_planted_analogue_in_each_of_the_four_sets_crashes(set_name):
    with pytest.raises(leakage.LeakageError, match=set_name):
        leakage.assert_no_leakage({"abaucin": ABAUCIN}, _sets(**{set_name: UNRELATED + [ANALOGUE]}))

def scaffold_split(scaffolds: list[str], labels: list[int], seed: int = SPLIT_SEED,
                   fractions: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Return a set name per molecule, keeping every scaffold group whole.

    Largest groups are placed first (a group bigger than the test share would otherwise be
    impossible to place late). The remaining groups are visited in a seeded random order,
    active-bearing groups first, and each goes to the set furthest below its target.
    """
    fractions = fractions or FRACTIONS
    n, n_pos = len(scaffolds), sum(labels)
    groups: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    for i, s in enumerate(scaffolds):
        groups[s].append(i)
    target_n = {k: v * n for k, v in fractions.items()}
    target_pos = {k: v * n_pos for k, v in fractions.items()}
    got_n = dict.fromkeys(fractions, 0)
    got_pos = dict.fromkeys(fractions, 0)
    assign = [""] * n

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    items = sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
    rng.shuffle(items)
    biggest = max(target_n.get("test", min(target_n.values())), 1)
    big = [g for g in items if len(g[1]) > biggest / 2]
    rest = [g for g in items if len(g[1]) <= biggest / 2]
    rest.sort(key=lambda g: 0 if any(labels[i] for i in g[1]) else 1)  # stable: active-bearing groups first

    def place(members: list[int], name: str) -> None:
        for i in members:
            assign[i] = name
        got_n[name] += len(members)

"""ROC-AUC, PR-AUC and stratified bootstrap intervals, in numpy only.

Plain accuracy is never reported: with 1.4% actives a model that says "inactive" to everything
scores 98.6%. ``baseline_prevalence`` (what a random ranker's PR-AUC converges to) is reported
beside every PR-AUC so the number can be read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def roc_auc(y: np.ndarray, score: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mann-Whitney form of ROC-AUC with average ranks for ties."""
    y, score = np.asarray(y), np.asarray(score, dtype=float)
    n_pos, n_neg = int((y == 1).sum()), int((y == 0).sum())
    if n_pos == 0 or n_neg == 0:
        return float("nan")
    order = np.argsort(score, kind="mergesort")
    ranks = np.empty(len(score))
    sorted_scores = score[order]
    i = 0
    while i < len(score):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(score) and sorted_scores[j + 1] == sorted_scores[i]:
            j += 1
        ranks[order[i:j + 1]] = (i + j) / 2.0 + 1.0
        i = j + 1
    return float((ranks[y == 1].sum() - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (n_pos * n_neg))

"""Each leakage control, tested by planting the leak it exists to catch."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from htb_wholecell import controls

ABAUCIN = "O=C1Nc2ccccc2C2(CCN(CCc3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)CC2)O1"
ANALOGUE = "O=C1Nc2ccccc2C2(CCN(CCc3ccc(C(F)(F)Cl)cc3)CC2)O1"      # CF3 -> CF2Cl, above 0.5
UNRELATED = ["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "CCCCCC(=O)O", "Cn1cnc2c1c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n2C",
             "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O", "NCCc1ccc(O)c(O)c1", "OCC1OC(O)C(O)C(O)C1O"]


def test_similarity_groups_keep_analogues_together_and_strangers_apart():
    groups = controls.similarity_groups([ABAUCIN, ANALOGUE, *UNRELATED])
    assert groups[0] == groups[1]
    assert len(set(groups[2:])) == len(UNRELATED) and groups[0] not in groups[2:]


def test_the_group_guarantee_holds_by_construction():
    # chain A-B-C: A~B and B~C are close, A~C may not be. Single linkage must still join all three.
    from rdkit import DataStructs

    from htb_wholecell import leakage
    chain = ["CCCCCCCCCC(=O)O", "CCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O", "CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O", "CCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O"]
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(chain, threshold=0.55)
    sims = [[DataStructs.TanimotoSimilarity(leakage.fingerprint(a), leakage.fingerprint(b)) for b in chain] for a in chain]
    for i in range(len(chain)):
        for j in range(len(chain)):
            if groups[i] != groups[j]:
                assert sims[i][j] < 0.55


def test_joint_groups_merge_on_a_shared_document_and_ignore_none():
    clusters = [0, 1, 2, 3]
    docs = ["d1", "d1", None, None]
    out = controls.joint_groups(clusters, docs)
    assert out[0] == out[1] and out[2] != out[3] and out[2] != out[0]


def test_joint_groups_chain_through_two_keys():
    out = controls.joint_groups([0, 0, 1, 2], ["a", None, "a", "z"])
    assert out[0] == out[1] == out[2] and out[3] != out[0]


def test_joint_groups_reject_ragged_input():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        controls.joint_groups([1, 2], ["a"])


def test_group_split_keeps_groups_whole_and_leaves_no_close_neighbour():
    smiles = [ABAUCIN, ANALOGUE, *UNRELATED] * 1
    labels = [1, 1] + [0] * len(UNRELATED)
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(smiles)
    assign = controls.group_split(groups, labels)
    assert assign[0] == assign[1]
    controls.assert_no_cross_split_neighbours(smiles, assign)


def test_a_planted_analogue_across_the_split_is_caught():
    smiles = [ABAUCIN, ANALOGUE, "CCO", "CCN"]
    with pytest.raises(controls.ControlError, match="training neighbour"):
        controls.assert_no_cross_split_neighbours(smiles, ["train", "test", "train", "test"])


def test_nearest_similarity_handles_an_empty_reference():
    assert controls.nearest_similarity(["CCO"], []).tolist() == [0.0]


def test_assert_disjoint_names_both_sets():
    controls.assert_disjoint("calibration", ["a", "b"], "test", ["c"])
    with pytest.raises(controls.ControlError, match="calibration and test"):
        controls.assert_disjoint("calibration", ["a", "b"], "test", ["b"])


def test_hash_split_is_deterministic_order_free_and_roughly_balanced():
    keys = [f"PRJ{i}" for i in range(400)]
    a, b = controls.hash_split(keys), controls.hash_split(list(reversed(keys)))
    assert a == b
    assert 0.4 < sum(v == "test" for v in a.values()) / len(a) < 0.6
    assert controls.hash_split(keys, seed=1) != a


def make_scores(n=600, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = rng.integers(0, 2, n)
    sim = rng.random(n)
    # memory: near compounds are scored almost perfectly, far ones are close to noise
    score = np.where(sim > 0.6, y + rng.normal(0, 0.1, n), rng.normal(0, 1, n) + 0.1 * y)
    return y, score, sim


def test_banded_report_partitions_the_data_and_exposes_memory():
    y, score, sim = make_scores()
    groups = np.arange(len(y))
    rep = controls.banded_report(y, score, sim, groups, n_boot=200)
    assert sum(b["n"] for b in rep["bands"]) == rep["all"]["n"] == len(y)
    near, far = rep["bands"][-1], rep["bands"][0]
    assert near["roc_auc"]["value"] > 0.95 > far["roc_auc"]["value"]


def test_cluster_bootstrap_is_wider_when_compounds_are_correlated():
    y, score, _ = make_scores(400)
    ci_single = controls.cluster_bootstrap(y, score, np.arange(400), controls.metrics.roc_auc, 300)
    ci_grouped = controls.cluster_bootstrap(y, score, np.arange(400) // 40, controls.metrics.roc_auc, 300)
    assert (ci_grouped[1] - ci_grouped[0]) > (ci_single[1] - ci_single[0])


def test_a_band_with_one_class_reports_no_auc_instead_of_a_number():
    rep = controls.banded_report([1, 1, 1, 0], [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.1], [0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.9], [0, 1, 2, 3], n_boot=20)
    assert rep["bands"][0]["roc_auc"] is None

"""Leakage audits over the artifacts the demo's numbers rest on.

    python -m eval.leakage_audit                  # every audit whose inputs exist
    python -m eval.leakage_audit --only ensemble  # one audit

Each audit returns a dict with a ``status``: ``pass``, ``fail`` (a hard leak: nothing downstream
should be quoted), ``warn`` (the number is real but flattering) or ``skipped`` (an input is missing,
and the reason is recorded, never hidden). The command exits 1 when any audit fails.

  ensemble      a trained ensemble's test set: calibration and test are disjoint, nothing in test is
                in training, and performance is reported by distance to the training set with
                intervals that resample whole similarity groups
  cluster_split what a similarity-group split of the same table would do to the near-neighbour
                share, written out as a split file; the sealed release is not touched
  ground_truth  whether the cited sources of the retrospective ground truth are documents whose
                MIC records feed the activity feature
  generated     whether a generated batch contains a held-out compound or a close analogue
  phenotype     whether a bioproject-level dev/test split of the susceptibility data is disjoint
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "results" / "leakage_audit"
MODEL = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "models" / "mic_573_scaffold"
RELEASE_573 = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "releases" / "chembl37_mic_taxon573"
RELEASE_LIU = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "releases" / "liu2023_hub20200324_chembl-37"
SURVIVORS = ROOT / "results" / "whole_cell" / "generated_run1" / "survivors.tsv"
GROUND_TRUTH = ROOT / "eval" / "ground_truth.json"
CHEMBL = ROOT / "data" / "chembl_extract" / "chembl_37" / "chembl_37_sqlite" / "chembl_37.db"
HELD_OUT_NAMES = ["RS-102895", "SU3327"]  # abaucin and halicin, the hidden-drug test's compounds
SEED = 20261108


def _read(path: Path, delimiter: str = "\t") -> list[dict]:
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=delimiter))


def _skipped(reason: str) -> dict:
    return {"status": "skipped", "reason": reason}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ensemble

def audit_ensemble(model_dir: Path = MODEL, n_boot: int = 1000) -> dict:
    from htb_wholecell import controls, leakage

    model_dir = Path(model_dir)
    needed = [model_dir / "predictions_test.tsv", model_dir / "predictions_calibration.tsv",
              model_dir / "member_0" / "train.csv"]
    missing = [str(p) for p in needed if not p.exists()]
    if missing:
        return _skipped("missing " + ", ".join(missing))
    test = _read(needed[0])
    cal = _read(needed[1])
    rows = _read(needed[2], ",")
    seen = [r for r in rows if r["split"] in ("train", "val")]
    problems = []
    try:
        controls.assert_disjoint("calibration", [r["inchikey"] for r in cal], "test", [r["inchikey"] for r in test])
        seen_keys = [leakage._key(r["smiles"]) for r in seen]
        controls.assert_disjoint("training", seen_keys, "test", [r["inchikey"] for r in test])
    except controls.ControlError as exc:
        problems.append(str(exc))

    smiles = [r["smiles"] for r in test]
    sim = controls.nearest_similarity(smiles, [r["smiles"] for r in seen])
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(smiles)
    y = np.array([int(r["label"]) for r in test])
    score = np.array([float(r["mean"]) for r in test])
    banded = controls.banded_report(y, score, sim, np.array(groups), n_boot=n_boot, seed=SEED)
    near = float((sim >= controls.THRESHOLD).mean())
    far = next(b for b in banded["bands"] if b["low"] == 0.0)
    status = "fail" if problems else ("warn" if near > 0.25 else "pass")
    return {"status": status, "problems": problems, "test_compounds": len(test),
            "share_with_training_neighbour_ge_0.5": round(near, 4), "median_nearest": round(float(np.median(sim)), 4),
            "test_group_sizes": controls.group_sizes(groups), "performance": banded,
            "reading": ("The overall figure includes compounds that have a close training analogue. "
                        "The 0.0-0.4 band is the estimate for new chemistry."),
            "far_band_roc_auc": far.get("roc_auc")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- cluster split

def audit_cluster_split(table: Path | None = None, out_dir: Path = OUT, threshold: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    from htb_wholecell import controls

    table = Path(table) if table else RELEASE_573 / "tables" / "mic_573.tsv"
    splits_path = table.with_name("splits.tsv")
    if not table.exists() or not splits_path.exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {table} or {splits_path}")
    rows = [r for r in _read(table) if r["label"] in ("0", "1")]
    old = {r["inchikey"]: r["scaffold_split"] for r in _read(splits_path)}
    smiles = [r["smiles"] for r in rows]
    labels = [int(r["label"]) for r in rows]
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(smiles, threshold)
    assign = controls.group_split(groups, labels)
    controls.assert_no_cross_split_neighbours(smiles, assign, threshold)  # raises on a leak

    def near_share(split_of) -> float | None:
        a = [split_of(r) for r in rows]
        test = [s for s, x in zip(smiles, a) if x == "test"]
        train = [s for s, x in zip(smiles, a) if x == "train"]
        if not test or not train:
            return None
        return round(float((controls.nearest_similarity(test, train) >= threshold).mean()), 4)

    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out_dir / "splits_cluster.tsv"
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        w = csv.writer(handle, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["inchikey", "similarity_group", "cluster_split", "scaffold_split"])
        for r, g, a in zip(rows, groups, assign):
            w.writerow([r["inchikey"], g, a, old.get(r["inchikey"], "")])
    counts = {name: assign.count(name) for name in ("train", "val", "test")}
    actives = {name: sum(l for l, a in zip(labels, assign) if a == name) for name in counts}
    return {"status": "pass", "threshold": threshold, "compounds": len(rows), "groups": controls.group_sizes(groups),
            "split_sizes": counts, "split_actives": actives,
            "test_share_with_training_neighbour": {"scaffold_split": near_share(lambda r: old.get(r["inchikey"])),
                                                   "similarity_group_split": 0.0},
            "written": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) if path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else str(path),
            "reading": ("A scaffold split leaves test compounds with close training analogues. The "
                        "similarity-group split guarantees none at or above the threshold, and asserts it. "
                        "Retrain on this file to get an estimate for new chemistry.")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ground truth

def audit_ground_truth(ground_truth: Path = GROUND_TRUTH, chembl: Path = CHEMBL) -> dict:
    ground_truth, chembl = Path(ground_truth), Path(chembl)
    if not ground_truth.exists() or not chembl.exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {ground_truth} or {chembl}")
    sources = json.loads(ground_truth.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["sources"]
    dois = sorted({s["id"].lower() for s in sources.values() if s.get("type") == "doi"} |
                  {s["doi"].lower() for s in sources.values() if s.get("doi")})
    pmids = sorted({int(s["pmid"]) for s in sources.values() if str(s.get("pmid", "")).isdigit()})
    with sqlite3.connect(chembl.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True) as db:
        docs = []
        for doi in dois:
            docs += db.execute("SELECT doc_id, doi, pubmed_id FROM docs WHERE lower(doi) = ?", (doi,)).fetchall()
        for pmid in pmids:
            docs += db.execute("SELECT doc_id, doi, pubmed_id FROM docs WHERE pubmed_id = ?", (pmid,)).fetchall()
        ids = sorted({d[0] for d in docs})
        mic = 0
        if ids:
            marks = ",".join("?" * len(ids))
            mic = db.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities WHERE standard_type = 'MIC' AND doc_id IN ({marks})",
                             ids).fetchone()[0]
    return {"status": "fail" if mic else "pass", "sources_checked": len(sources), "dois": len(dois), "pmids": len(pmids),
            "chembl_documents_matched": len(ids), "mic_records_in_those_documents": mic,
            "reading": ("No cited source is a ChEMBL document with MIC records, so the activity feature does not "
                        "contain the ground-truth sources' own measurements. The guidelines themselves summarise MIC "
                        "and clinical evidence, so activity and ground truth are not independent in substance."
                        if not mic else "Some cited sources are ChEMBL documents with MIC records: exclude them.")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- generated

def audit_generated(survivors: Path = SURVIVORS, release: Path = RELEASE_LIU, names=HELD_OUT_NAMES) -> dict:
    survivors, release = Path(survivors), Path(release)
    if not survivors.exists() or not (release / "tables" / "hub_pool.tsv").exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {survivors} or {release}/tables/hub_pool.tsv")
    from htb_wholecell import generate, leakage

    held = generate.held_out_smiles(release, list(names))
    members = [r["smiles"] for r in _read(survivors)]
    sets = {name: [] for name in leakage.REQUIRED_SETS}
    sets["generated_batch"] = members
    leaks = leakage.find_leaks(held, sets)
    return {"status": "fail" if leaks else "pass", "held_out": sorted(held), "generated_molecules": len(members),
            "leaks": [{"held_out": x.held_out, "member": x.member, "similarity": x.similarity} for x in leaks],
            "reading": "Checked after generation; the same assertion also runs before it on the guide model's inputs."}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- phenotype

def audit_phenotype(data_dir: Path | None = None, test_fraction: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    from htb_wholecell import controls

    from eval import phenotype_validation as pv

    data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else pv.DATA
    if not (data_dir / pv.SPECIES["klebsiella"][1]).exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {data_dir}")
    isolates, _ = pv.load_isolates(data_dir)
    split = controls.hash_split([i["cluster"] for i in isolates], test_fraction, SEED)
    dev = {i["biosample"] for i in isolates if split[i["cluster"]] == "dev"}
    test = {i["biosample"] for i in isolates if split[i["cluster"]] == "test"}
    controls.assert_disjoint("dev isolates", dev, "test isolates", test)
    by_species = {}
    for key in pv.SPECIES:
        mine = [i for i in isolates if i["species"] == key]
        by_species[key] = {"dev": sum(split[i["cluster"]] == "dev" for i in mine),
                           "test": sum(split[i["cluster"]] == "test" for i in mine),
                           "bioprojects": len({i["cluster"] for i in mine})}
    lopsided = [k for k, v in by_species.items() if min(v["dev"], v["test"]) < 0.2 * (v["dev"] + v["test"])]
    return {"status": "warn" if lopsided else "pass", "isolates": len(isolates), "by_species": by_species,
            "lopsided_species": lopsided,
            "reading": ("Isolates from one bioproject are never on both sides. A species dominated by one bioproject "
                        "cannot be split evenly by study; use dev/test only for anything tuned after the frozen run.")}


AUDITS = {"ensemble": audit_ensemble, "cluster_split": audit_cluster_split, "ground_truth": audit_ground_truth,
          "generated": audit_generated, "phenotype": audit_phenotype}


def run(only: list[str] | None = None, out_dir: Path = OUT) -> dict:
    results = {}
    for name, fn in AUDITS.items():
        if only and name not in only:
            continue
        try:
            results[name] = fn() if name != "cluster_split" else fn(out_dir=out_dir)
        except AssertionError as exc:  # a control raised: that is a failed audit, not a crash
            results[name] = {"status": "fail", "problems": [str(exc)]}
    return {"schema": 1, "run_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "audits": results}


def as_markdown(report: dict) -> str:
    lines = ["# Leakage audit", "", "| Audit | Status | Note |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for name, r in report["audits"].items():
        note = r.get("reason") or "; ".join(r.get("problems", [])) or r.get("reading", "")
        lines.append(f"| {name} | **{r['status']}** | {note[:140]} |")
    ens = report["audits"].get("ensemble", {})
    if "performance" in ens:
        p = ens["performance"]
        lines += ["", f"## Ensemble by distance to the training set ({ens['test_compounds']} test compounds, "
                  f"{100 * ens['share_with_training_neighbour_ge_0.5']:.0f}% have a neighbour at or above 0.5)", "",
                  "| Nearest training Tanimoto | n | actives | ROC-AUC (95% CI over groups) | PR-AUC |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for label, b in [("all", p["all"]), *[(f"{x['low']:.1f}-{x['high']:.1f}", x) for x in p["bands"]]]:
            roc = b.get("roc_auc")
            lines.append(f"| {label} | {b['n']} | {b['actives']} | "
                         + (f"{roc['value']:.3f} ({roc['ci95'][0]:.3f}-{roc['ci95'][1]:.3f})" if roc else "n/a") + " | "
                         + (f"{b['pr_auc']['value']:.3f}" if b.get("pr_auc") else "n/a") + " |")
    cs = report["audits"].get("cluster_split", {})
    if cs.get("status") == "pass":
        lines += ["", "## Similarity-group split", "", f"{cs['compounds']} compounds in {cs['groups']['groups']} groups "
                  f"(largest {100 * cs['groups']['largest_share']:.0f}%). Test compounds with a training neighbour "
                  f"at or above {cs['threshold']}: scaffold split "
                  f"{100 * (cs['test_share_with_training_neighbour']['scaffold_split'] or 0):.0f}%, group split 0%. "
                  f"Written to `{cs['written']}`."]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m eval.leakage_audit", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--only", nargs="+", choices=sorted(AUDITS))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    report = run(args.only, args.out)
    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (args.out / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (args.out / "report.md").write_text(as_markdown(report), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(as_markdown(report))
    return 1 if any(r["status"] == "fail" for r in report["audits"].values()) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Leakage audits over the artifacts the demo's numbers rest on.

    python -m eval.leakage_audit                  # every audit whose inputs exist
    python -m eval.leakage_audit --only ensemble  # one audit

Each audit returns a dict with a ``status``: ``pass``, ``fail`` (a hard leak: nothing downstream
should be quoted), ``warn`` (the number is real but flattering) or ``skipped`` (an input is missing,
and the reason is recorded, never hidden). The command exits 1 when any audit fails.

  ensemble      a trained ensemble's test set: calibration and test are disjoint, nothing in test is
                in training, and performance is reported by distance to the training set with
                intervals that resample whole similarity groups
  cluster_split what a similarity-group split of the same table would do to the near-neighbour
                share, written out as a split file; the sealed release is not touched
  ground_truth  whether the cited sources of the retrospective ground truth are documents whose
                MIC records feed the activity feature
  generated     whether a generated batch contains a held-out compound or a close analogue
  phenotype     whether a bioproject-level dev/test split of the susceptibility data is disjoint
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "results" / "leakage_audit"
MODEL = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "models" / "mic_573_scaffold"
RELEASE_573 = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "releases" / "chembl37_mic_taxon573"
RELEASE_LIU = ROOT / "data" / "wholecell" / "releases" / "liu2023_hub20200324_chembl-37"
SURVIVORS = ROOT / "results" / "whole_cell" / "generated_run1" / "survivors.tsv"
GROUND_TRUTH = ROOT / "eval" / "ground_truth.json"
CHEMBL = ROOT / "data" / "chembl_extract" / "chembl_37" / "chembl_37_sqlite" / "chembl_37.db"
HELD_OUT_NAMES = ["RS-102895", "SU3327"]  # abaucin and halicin, the hidden-drug test's compounds
SEED = 20261108


def _read(path: Path, delimiter: str = "\t") -> list[dict]:
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=delimiter))


def _skipped(reason: str) -> dict:
    return {"status": "skipped", "reason": reason}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ensemble

def audit_ensemble(model_dir: Path = MODEL, n_boot: int = 1000) -> dict:
    from htb_wholecell import controls, leakage

    model_dir = Path(model_dir)
    needed = [model_dir / "predictions_test.tsv", model_dir / "predictions_calibration.tsv",
              model_dir / "member_0" / "train.csv"]
    missing = [str(p) for p in needed if not p.exists()]
    if missing:
        return _skipped("missing " + ", ".join(missing))
    test = _read(needed[0])
    cal = _read(needed[1])
    rows = _read(needed[2], ",")
    seen = [r for r in rows if r["split"] in ("train", "val")]
    problems = []
    try:
        controls.assert_disjoint("calibration", [r["inchikey"] for r in cal], "test", [r["inchikey"] for r in test])
        seen_keys = [leakage._key(r["smiles"]) for r in seen]
        controls.assert_disjoint("training", seen_keys, "test", [r["inchikey"] for r in test])
    except controls.ControlError as exc:
        problems.append(str(exc))

    smiles = [r["smiles"] for r in test]
    sim = controls.nearest_similarity(smiles, [r["smiles"] for r in seen])
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(smiles)
    y = np.array([int(r["label"]) for r in test])
    score = np.array([float(r["mean"]) for r in test])
    banded = controls.banded_report(y, score, sim, np.array(groups), n_boot=n_boot, seed=SEED)
    near = float((sim >= controls.THRESHOLD).mean())
    far = next(b for b in banded["bands"] if b["low"] == 0.0)
    status = "fail" if problems else ("warn" if near > 0.25 else "pass")
    return {"status": status, "problems": problems, "test_compounds": len(test),
            "share_with_training_neighbour_ge_0.5": round(near, 4), "median_nearest": round(float(np.median(sim)), 4),
            "test_group_sizes": controls.group_sizes(groups), "performance": banded,
            "reading": ("The overall figure includes compounds that have a close training analogue. "
                        "The 0.0-0.4 band is the estimate for new chemistry."),
            "far_band_roc_auc": far.get("roc_auc")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- cluster split

def audit_cluster_split(table: Path | None = None, out_dir: Path = OUT, threshold: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    from htb_wholecell import controls

    table = Path(table) if table else RELEASE_573 / "tables" / "mic_573.tsv"
    splits_path = table.with_name("splits.tsv")
    if not table.exists() or not splits_path.exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {table} or {splits_path}")
    rows = [r for r in _read(table) if r["label"] in ("0", "1")]
    old = {r["inchikey"]: r["scaffold_split"] for r in _read(splits_path)}
    smiles = [r["smiles"] for r in rows]
    labels = [int(r["label"]) for r in rows]
    groups = controls.similarity_groups(smiles, threshold)
    assign = controls.group_split(groups, labels)
    controls.assert_no_cross_split_neighbours(smiles, assign, threshold)  # raises on a leak

    def near_share(split_of) -> float | None:
        a = [split_of(r) for r in rows]
        test = [s for s, x in zip(smiles, a) if x == "test"]
        train = [s for s, x in zip(smiles, a) if x == "train"]
        if not test or not train:
            return None
        return round(float((controls.nearest_similarity(test, train) >= threshold).mean()), 4)

    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out_dir / "splits_cluster.tsv"
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        w = csv.writer(handle, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["inchikey", "similarity_group", "cluster_split", "scaffold_split"])
        for r, g, a in zip(rows, groups, assign):
            w.writerow([r["inchikey"], g, a, old.get(r["inchikey"], "")])
    counts = {name: assign.count(name) for name in ("train", "val", "test")}
    actives = {name: sum(l for l, a in zip(labels, assign) if a == name) for name in counts}
    return {"status": "pass", "threshold": threshold, "compounds": len(rows), "groups": controls.group_sizes(groups),
            "split_sizes": counts, "split_actives": actives,
            "test_share_with_training_neighbour": {"scaffold_split": near_share(lambda r: old.get(r["inchikey"])),
                                                   "similarity_group_split": 0.0},
            "written": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) if path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else str(path),
            "reading": ("A scaffold split leaves test compounds with close training analogues. The "
                        "similarity-group split guarantees none at or above the threshold, and asserts it. "
                        "Retrain on this file to get an estimate for new chemistry.")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ground truth

def audit_ground_truth(ground_truth: Path = GROUND_TRUTH, chembl: Path = CHEMBL) -> dict:
    ground_truth, chembl = Path(ground_truth), Path(chembl)
    if not ground_truth.exists() or not chembl.exists():
        return _skipped(f"missing {ground_truth} or {chembl}")
    sources = json.loads(ground_truth.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["sources"]
    dois = sorted({s["id"].lower() for s in sources.values() if s.get("type") == "doi"} |
                  {s["doi"].lower() for s in sources.values() if s.get("doi")})
    pmids = sorted({int(s["pmid"]) for s in sources.values() if str(s.get("pmid", "")).isdigit()})
    with sqlite3.connect(chembl.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True) as db:
        docs = []
        for doi in dois:
            docs += db.execute("SELECT doc_id, doi, pubmed_id FROM docs WHERE lower(doi) = ?", (doi,)).fetchall()
        for pmid in pmids:
            docs += db.execute("SELECT doc_id, doi, pubmed_id FROM docs WHERE pubmed_id = ?", (pmid,)).fetchall()
        ids = sorted({d[0] for d in docs})
        mic = 0
        if ids:
            marks = ",".join("?" * len(ids))
            mic = db.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities WHERE standard_type = 'MIC' AND doc_id IN ({marks})",
                             ids).fetchone()[0]
    return {"status": "fail" if mic else "pass", "sources_checked": len(sources), "dois": len(dois), "pmids": len(pmids),
            "chembl_documents_matched": len(ids), "mic_records_in_those_documents": mic,
            "reading": ("No cited source is a ChEMBL document with MIC records, so the activity feature does not "
                        "contain the ground-truth sources' own measurements. The guidelines themselves summarise MIC "
                        "and clinical evidence, so activity and ground truth are not independent in substance."
                        if not mic else "Some cited sources are ChEMBL documents with MIC records: exclude them.")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- generated

def audit_generated(survivors: Path = SURVIVORS, release: Path = RELEASE_LIU, names=HELD_OUT_NAMES) -> dict:
    survivors, release = Path(survivors), Path(release)
    if not survivors.exists() or not (release / "tables" / "hub_pool.tsv").exists():

            "leaks": [{"held_out": x.held_out, "member": x.member, "similarity": x.similarity} for x in leaks],
            "reading": "Checked after generation; the same assertion also runs before it on the guide model's inputs."}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- phenotype

                           "test": sum(split[i["cluster"]] == "test" for i in mine),
                           "bioprojects": len({i["cluster"] for i in mine})}
    lopsided = [k for k, v in by_species.items() if min(v["dev"], v["test"]) < 0.2 * (v["dev"] + v["test"])]
    return {"status": "warn" if lopsided else "pass", "isolates": len(isolates), "by_species": by_species,
            "lopsided_species": lopsided,
            "reading": ("Isolates from one bioproject are never on both sides. A species dominated by one bioproject "
                        "cannot be split evenly by study; use dev/test only for anything tuned after the frozen run.")}


AUDITS = {"ensemble": audit_ensemble, "cluster_split": audit_cluster_split, "ground_truth": audit_ground_truth,
          "generated": audit_generated, "phenotype": audit_phenotype}
